clue.text: Happy after pawn's taken in game

indicators.note: 'after' says the word for happy is placed behind the chess piece's letter rather than before it

parts.note: P is the chess notation for a pawn
happy in the sense of fortunate

explanation.surface: A chess player cheers up after capturing a pawn during a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' looks like the chess match, but it is the definition: game as an adjective means brave and willing.
explanation.definitionFit: Game as an adjective means spirited and ready to have a go, a synonym of brave.

clue.text: Deeply significant, as expert discovered

parts.note: a pro is a professional, an expert
simple synonym

explanation.surface: An expert has uncovered something of real importance.
explanation.definitionFit: Something profound has great depth of meaning, a synonym for deeply significant.

clue.text: Without any reservations for express

definitions.meaning: first meaning: complete, absolute, as an adjective
second meaning: to say aloud or voice, as a verb

explanation.surface: Something available without booking for an express train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reservations' and 'express' suggest train travel; the adjective sense (utter nonsense) and the verb sense (utter a word) are unrelated.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means total and unqualified; as a verb it means to speak or give voice to.

clue.text: Writer having half a fish for breakfast, then another

indicators.note: 'half' means only one of the two halves of the fish's name is kept, the rest discarded

parts.note: a kipper is a smoked herring, a traditional British breakfast
another fish: ling is a long cod-like sea fish

explanation.surface: An author has half a fish at breakfast and then eats a second one.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half of KIPPER is KIP; 'another' means another fish, giving LING.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudyard Kipling was the English author of The Jungle Book and Kim, so he is an example of a writer.

clue.text: Heroic changes for person who'll likewise succeed?

indicators.note: 'changes' tells us the word before it is altered into a different arrangement of its letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Heroic transformations happen to someone who will also triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'succeed' here means to follow into an inheritance, not to be successful; the question mark flags that pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A co-heir shares an inheritance, so they inherit, or succeed to the estate, jointly with another heir.

clue.text: Emerge with parts switched, as result

indicators.note: the phrase tells us the two halves of the phrase for emerge swap places, front going to the back

parts.note: to come out is to emerge

explanation.surface: Something emerges with its components rearranged, producing a result.
explanation.walkthrough: COME OUT becomes OUT COME when its two words change places.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcome is the consequence or end result of something.

clue.text: Fight opponents at bridge with noble monarch

parts.note: East and North sit on opposing sides at a bridge table
a count is a nobleman
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword monarch

explanation.surface: A battle with rivals at the card table, a nobleman and a king involved.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, North-South play against East-West, so any pair like E and N are opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: An encounter can be a battle or clash between hostile forces, so it is a synonym of fight.

clue.text: Resistance over crackpot ideas brought up

indicators.note: in a down clue 'over' means placed above, so the first piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance

indicators.note: crackpot means crazy, so the word after it is scrambled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Opposition to some wild notions was mentioned in discussion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crackpot ideas' reads as a single phrase, but crackpot is the signal to rearrange ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring up a subject is to raise it, so brought up and raised are synonyms in the past tense.

clue.text: What's up, possibly, outside ring for unusual boxer

indicators.note: 'outside' tells us the shuffled letters wrap around the next item
'possibly' suggests the phrase before it is one possible arrangement among others

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A spectator wonders what is going on outside the boxing ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' looks like part of the boxing scene but just supplies a circle-shaped letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A southpaw is a left-handed boxer, who leads with the right and is less common than orthodox fighters.

clue.text: Weapon for jet fighter?

parts.note: surface reading: armament carried by a military jet plane
setter's reading: someone who fights with jets of liquid, a child's toy gun that squirts

explanation.walkthrough: A jet fighter suggests a military aircraft, but here it is anyone fighting by squirting jets.
explanation.definitionFit: A toy gun that shoots a stream of liquid is the weapon of someone who battles with jets of spray.

clue.text: In first act, I carefully established plan for play

indicators.note: 'In' tells us the letters sit inside the words that follow, running across them

parts.note: found across the end of first, all of act and I, and the start of carefully

explanation.surface: A dramatist describes how the opening act set up the plot with care.
explanation.definitionFit: A tactic is a planned manoeuvre, especially a scheme for how to play a game or match.

clue.text: Low river berth

parts.note: to low is to make the sound of cattle
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A mooring spot on a river at low water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' looks like an adjective about the river level, but it is the cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: To berth a boat is to secure it in a dock, which is what mooring a vessel means.

clue.text: At home, somehow courted daughter and proposed

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: 'somehow' says the next word gets there in some undefined way, so its letters are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A suitor courted the daughter at her family home and then popped the question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'proposed' wants to be about marriage, but it is the formal sense of putting a motion forward.
explanation.definitionFit: To introduce a bill or motion is to put it forward for consideration, the same as proposing it.

clue.text: Aim to irritate people ahead of time, creating hazard

indicators.note: 'ahead of' places the word for people in front of the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal
to anger is to irritate
simple synonym
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Deliberately annoying people too early causes danger.
explanation.definitionFit: Endangerment is the act of putting someone at risk, which a hazard does.

clue.text: A politician was untruthful about condition being strengthened

indicators.note: 'about' says the verb for lying goes around the word for condition

parts.note: taken as written
a Member of Parliament
told a lie
if introduces a condition

explanation.surface: An MP lied about a health condition that was said to be improving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'condition' suggests health, but it is the little word that introduces a condition in grammar, as in 'only if'.
explanation.definitionFit: Amplified means made louder or greater, so it is a synonym of strengthened.

clue.text: One thing female tries to dispose of on beach? It's hard to say!

definitions.text: One thing female tries to dispose of on beach? It's hard to say!

parts.words: One thing female tries to dispose of on beach?
parts.note: surface reading: litter a woman wants to get rid of at the seaside
setter's reading: the tongue-twister 'She sells ... on the seashore', where she disposes of her wares by selling

explanation.walkthrough: 'dispose of' here means sell, and 'hard to say' points to the famous English tongue-twister about a woman selling shells by the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: In the tongue-twister she sells them by the sea, so a single one is the thing she tries to sell.

clue.text: Setting English novelist, as announced, for part of course

parts.note: putting something down is setting it

indicators.note: 'as announced' says we want the sound of the novelist's name when spoken, not its spelling

parts.note: Graham Greene, English author of Brighton Rock

explanation.surface: Putting a novelist's work into some context, as reported, for a literature course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' suggests study, but it is a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: A putting green is the closely mown area around each hole on a golf course.

clue.text: Member of staff a head interrupts after start of term, mostly

indicators.note: something that interrupts breaks into the middle of something else
'mostly' means most but not all of the word is used, so its last letter goes

parts.note: taken as written
a head means per person, each

explanation.surface: A staff member is interrupted by the headteacher just after the school term begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' suggests a headteacher, but 'a head' means apiece, as in prices of so much a head.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacher is one of the staff of a school, so is a member of staff.

clue.text: Supporter in camp is fellow central European?

parts.note: simple synonym

indicators.note: 'central' means only the middle letters of the next word are kept

parts.note: the middle four letters of the word

explanation.surface: A fellow from central Europe is a supporter at the campsite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporter' suggests a fan, but it is the line holding up a tent.
explanation.definitionFit: A guy rope is a line pegged to the ground that holds up a tent at a campsite.

clue.text: Film, for instance that's neither rare nor well done

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a means of artistic expression, such as film
second meaning: a steak cooked to a middle degree

explanation.surface: A film reviewer finds a movie only average, neither undercooked nor polished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rare' and 'well done' sound like praise, but they are degrees of cooking steak.
explanation.definitionFit: Film is an artistic medium; a steak cooked between rare and well done is ordered medium.

clue.text: Hat in style in certain fashion — or not

indicators.note: to fashion something is to shape it, so the letters before it are remade into a new form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Wearing a hat stylishly in a particular way, or perhaps not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashion' does double duty, signalling the rearrangement and completing the definition: doing something in a certain manner, or rather not certain.
explanation.definitionFit: To act hesitantly is to act uncertainly, so in a manner that is certain — or rather not certain.

clue.text: This part of body is in foot? Yes and no

indicators.note: 'in' places the first word inside the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: FT is the abbreviation for foot
taken as written
surface padding: a joking comment that the word really is inside

explanation.surface: Is this body part found in the foot? Both yes and no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yes and no' is the joke: the letters of 'is' really are in the abbreviation for foot, but a fist is a hand, not part of a foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A fist is a clenched hand, a part of the human body.

clue.text: Deceptive move by boxer that's weak, we hear

indicators.note: 'we hear' says the word is identified by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: faint means weak or feeble

explanation.surface: A boxer's trick move turns out to be a feeble one, or so we're told.
explanation.definitionFit: A feint is a pretended blow that draws the opponent's guard before the real punch.

clue.text: School embracing popular conclusion

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so one word wraps around the other

parts.note: a school is a group of fish
in means fashionable, popular

explanation.surface: A school taking up a popular end to the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' suggests education, but it is a shoal of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A finish is an ending, so it is a noun synonym of conclusion.

clue.text: Celebrated British rugby player transformed side

parts.note: the British and Irish Lions are a touring rugby team

indicators.note: something transformed has been changed in form, so the next word's letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A famous British rugby international changed the team's fortunes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'side' looks like a team, but it is just letters to rearrange. A Lion is a player picked for the combined British and Irish rugby touring team.
explanation.definitionFit: To lionise someone is to treat them as a celebrity, so lionised means celebrated.

clue.text: New way to introduce service

indicators.note: to introduce something is to come before it, so the first piece is put in front

parts.note: a mode is a way or manner
RN, the Royal Navy, known as the Senior Service

explanation.surface: A fresh method for bringing in a new church or business service.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Navy is Britain's oldest armed service, so 'service' often gives RN.
explanation.definitionFit: Modern means up to date or recent, a synonym of new.

clue.text: Lead, perhaps, holding end of mission in mind

indicators.note: something holding another item contains it, wrapped around it

parts.note: lead is an example of a metal

indicators.note: 'end of' keeps only the final letter of the following word

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A team leader keeps the goal of the operation in their thoughts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' wants to be the verb or a leader, but it is the heavy metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Mental describes what happens inside the mind, so it means in mind as an adjectival phrase.
